profile_md: Provision found so far at Essex is led by **iTeams**, an extracurricular programme run by Essex Startups in which multidisciplinary student teams tackle challenges set by external businesses, mentored by industry experts, and present a report and pitch to a panel. It is selective (limited places, application), not credit-bearing as evidenced, and the latest evidenced edition is February 2025 (7 weeks, three businesses, six teams); a bespoke Cyber Innovate to Elevate variant connecting MSc/PhD students with SMEs ran to February 2026 but its team structure and outputs are not confirmed. Within Essex Business School, the Marketing Management module has students undertake a consultancy project for a real-world business, but whether this is group-based and how clients participate is not established; the MBA consultancy project is individual. Computer Science has a team project module without external clients and an individual capstone that can use company briefs. The Industry and Placements team promotes employer-led project briefs and live-project work-based learning (cited on Science and Health degree pages) but specific modules were not identified. The Big Essex Award is an employability award, excluded. Essex Law School runs team-based clinics: the Business Law Clinic (final-year LLB/PGT teams, 2025-26 projects with the Mercury Theatre and credit unions) and the Human Rights Centre Clinic (supervised teams working with NGOs/international bodies, HU902, six projects in 2026/27). Engineering, science and arts/social science searches found only individual capstones or unspecified WBL options. Provision is distributed (extracurricular central, Law clinics, one Business School module) rather than institution-wide, and none is yet verified as meeting all three criteria with current delivery.
gaps: Further departmental instances likely (Health, Nursing, Economics, Art History not searched in depth). iTeams 2025/26 not confirmed; Marketing Management group/client status unknown; Business Law Clinic credit and partner coverage unclear; Human Rights Clinic partner role unclear; WBL project modules unidentified. Reduced-depth review.
